title: Distal Radius Fracture Rehabilitation
case: Presentation (from the chapter): Stiff wrist and forearm (especially supination and extension), stiff fingers if not exercised. Weak grip, swelling, pain with loading.
plan: Track wrist and forearm range, grip strength (percentage of other side), PRWE. Refer older patients for bone health and falls prevention (Vol 11 Ch 4 and 5).
qa: Why move the fingers during casting? To prevent finger stiffness and swelling, which are major causes of poor outcome.
What is CRPS and why act early? A disproportionate pain condition with vasomotor and trophic changes; early recognition and graded activity improve outcomes.
Which motion is often slowest to return? Supination and wrist extension.
Sudden inability to lift the thumb weeks after fracture? Possible EPL rupture; refer.
What else should an older patient receive? Falls prevention and bone health assessment.

manual.name: Radiocarpal and midcarpal glides
manual.finding: Dorsal glide for flexion, palmar glide for extension, grades III to IV

manual.name: Oedema massage (retrograde)
manual.finding: Fingertips toward the elbow, with elevation

exercise.Exercise: Tendon gliding, thumb opposition, shoulder and elbow range, elevation
Active wrist flexion and extension, radial and ulnar deviation, forearm rotation with a hammer, composite fist
Putty grip, wrist curls with light weight, weight-bearing through the hand on a table
Carrying, opening jars, push-up progressions, work and hobby tasks

modalityNotes: Heat before exercise for stiffness; contrast baths not essential. Splints may be used for support or for stretching stiff joints as advised.
